sections.title: Sound of letter Y
paragraphs: The name of this letter is (Y) /waɪ/. Its main sound is heard in (yes) /jɛs/, which shows agreement. This letter makes four different sounds in English words.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: First, lift the middle of your tongue high near the roof of your mouth. Your lips spread wide and your voice turns on. Put a hand on your throat to feel it shake. Next, keep the tongue high and front for a short vowel. Then, glide from an open mouth up toward a close sound. Last, keep your tongue slightly lower and relaxed.

sections.title: Spelling rules
paragraphs: At the start of a syllable before a vowel, it sounds like (yellow) /jɛl.oʊ/. When unstressed at the end of a word or syllable, it sounds like (happy) /hæp.i/. In a stressed open syllable or at the end of a short word, it sounds like (fly) /flaɪ/. In a closed syllable, it sounds like (gym) /dʒɪm/.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not turn the beginning sound into a hard friction or a burst of air. Keep the air flowing smoothly without touching the roof of your mouth. Also, do not say the end of words like (city) /sɪt.i/ with a diphthong like the vowel in my. Keep that final vowel short and steady.
